source.name: When the focused control inside a focus trap removes itself, focus must stay inside the trap
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/focus-trap/focus-trap/pull/932) at 0eca669477eb3e25c197809efbbbd8fc451eb346. Blind to the maintainers' fix fce60b3a737759c6e0e787d3fa1603f2cb86300a; routing auto.

journey.title: Focus stays in the results dialog after Show all removes itself
journey.goal: Activating a control that removes itself keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

functionalJourney.title: Show all results with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, lists every result and closes

guards.title: Escape closes results and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: The Show all button removes itself while it is focused, causing focus to leave the dialog and the focus trap not restoring focus because the active element is gone.
plan.repair_strategy: Move focus to another focusable element inside the dialog (the close button) before removing the Show all button, ensuring focus remains trapped.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard focus remains inside the dialog after activating Show all, allowing continued tab navigation within the dialog.
functional_risks: Focusing the close button may be unexpected but still logical; if the close button were hidden or disabled it would be problematic, but it is visible and enabled.
Accidentally activating the close button with Enter is possible but requires an additional key press, preserving intended behavior.
verification_requirements: After activating Show all, focus is on the close button (or another element inside the dialog).
Subsequent Tab moves focus to the next trap element (e.g., first list item) and Shift+Tab moves to previous trap element.
The Show all button is removed from the DOM.
The count updates to '4 of 4 results'.
